definition: Classifying an entire 3D point cloud — e.g.
details: Classifying an entire 3D point cloud — e.g. chair vs. table in LiDAR scans — with architectures like PointNet and point transformers.

explainer.lead: 3D point cloud classification gives a whole collection of 3D points one object label, such as chair or table. It lets software recognize what a LiDAR scan contains instead of treating the scan as an unlabeled cloud of coordinates.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a connect-the-dots drawing made from dots floating in space. Instead of naming each dot, the computer looks at all of them together and says, "This is a chair" or "This is a table."
tiers.practitioner: Use it when the desired output is one class per point cloud, with architectures such as PointNet or point transformers processing the 3D points. A common setup is classifying objects in LiDAR scans; do not confuse this single cloud-level prediction with assigning a class to every point.
tiers.paperLevel: Given P = {p_i}_{i=1}^N, where p_i in R^3, the task is to learn f(P) -> y, with y denoting one class for the entire cloud. PointNet and point transformers are architectures used for this task, which is distinct from producing a separate output for each p_i.

explainer.example: A LiDAR scan of a chair produces a cloud of 3D points. The model processes the entire cloud and outputs "chair" rather than "table," assigning that single label to the scan.

usedIn.name: LiDAR scan analysis
usedIn.detail: Recognizing scanned objects, such as distinguishing chairs from tables.

usedIn.name: Indoor object recognition
usedIn.detail: Assigning an object category to a complete 3D scan rather than labeling its individual points.

explainer.intuition: Individual 3D points reveal little on their own, but together they describe an object. Classification combines evidence from the whole cloud into a single category.
howItWorks: Start with a set of 3D points representing one object.
Process the points with an architecture such as PointNet or a point transformer.
Combine information across the cloud into a representation of the whole object.
Predict one class label for that object.
explainer.whyItMatters: It turns raw 3D measurements into object categories that software can use. This provides a direct way to recognize whole objects represented by point clouds.
misconceptions: It does not assign a separate class to every point; it assigns one class to the entire cloud.
A point cloud is not a labeled object by itself; a classifier must infer the category from its points.

nodes.label: Object class
nodes.note: One label, such as chair or table
